public_rationale: OpenAI's reported first-half revenue does not settle its September ceiling. Anthropic's filing provides significant contrary context: quarterly figures total $2.545 billion through September 30. But that is a day beyond the stated cutoff, and the accounting basis is not reconciled to the estimate. The run-rate disclosure cannot replace realized revenue, and the combined cash-burn assertions remain unverified. The full compound claim is therefore unresolved.
limitations: Treating September 30 as equivalent to September 29 could change the result; that substitution is not made.
The public schema provides one contract metric scope, so revenue is the principal scope and cash burn is separately specified in the criteria.
Some OpenAI evidence is secondary reporting of inaccessible private disclosures.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI seem a little lethargic, both burning billions while making, by his estimates, no more than $2 billion and $6.26 billion respectively in 2025 so far, against full-year projections of $5 billion and $13 billion.

statement.excerpt: Even Anthropic and OpenAI seem a little lethargic, both burning billions of dollars while making, by my estimates, no more than $2 billion and $6.26 billion in 2025 so far, despite projections of $5 billion and $13 billion respectively.

from_speaker: no more than $2 billion and $6.26 billion
projections of $5 billion and $13 billion respectively
our_interpretation: The revenue amounts map respectively to Anthropic and OpenAI.
2025 so far means January 1 through September 29, 2025, the publication date.
The main metric scope records realized revenue. Cash burn and the existence of the stated full-year forecasts are separate components requiring their own measures.
Burning billions means at least $2 billion of net cash consumption per company during the stated year-to-date period; it does not mean accounting net losses.
The description seem a little lethargic is subjective commentary and is not separately graded.
The basis is estimate because Zitron expressly labels the figures his estimates. The treatment of reseller revenue is not specified.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish revenue through September 29 of no more than $2 billion for Anthropic and $6.26 billion for OpenAI, cash burn of at least $2 billion each, and the stated contemporaneous full-year forecasts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish that either company exceeded its revenue ceiling by September 29, that either cash-burn assertion is false, or that the stated forecast was materially misrepresented. A partial-period figure below a ceiling cannot establish the full-period ceiling.
